title: Weekly Initial Unemployment Claims Increase to 235,000
content: The U.S. Department of Labor reported that in the week ending August 16, the advance figure for seasonally adjusted initial unemployment claims rose to 235,000, an increase of 11,000 from the previous week’s unrevised level of 224,000. The 4‑week moving average of weekly claims was 226,250, up 4,500 from the prior week’s unrevised average of 221,750. Both the weekly figure and the moving average were above the consensus forecast.

title: Weekly Initial Unemployment Claims Increase to 237,000
content: The U.S. Department of Labor reported that in the week ending August 30, 2025 the seasonally adjusted initial unemployment claims rose to 237,000, an increase of 8,000 from the previous week’s unrevised figure of 229,000. The 4‑week moving average of weekly claims was 231,000, up 2,500 from the prior week’s unrevised average of 228,500. The data, which were released by Calculated Risk, also noted that weekly claims exceeded the consensus forecast. The accompanying graph shows the 4‑week moving average of weekly claims since 1971, with the current average highlighted by a dashed line.

title: Weekly Initial Unemployment Claims Increase to 263,000; Highest Since 2021
content: The U.S. Department of Labor reported that in the week ending September 6, 2025, the advance figure for seasonally adjusted initial jobless claims rose to 263,000, up 27,000 from the previous week’s revised level of 236,000. This is the highest level since October 23, 2021, when claims were 268,000. The 4‑week moving average increased to 240,500, up 9,750 from the prior revised average of 230,750. The weekly claims were well above the consensus forecast.

title: Weekly Initial Unemployment Claims Decrease to 229,000
content: The U.S. Department of Labor reported that in the week ending August 23, the advance figure for seasonally adjusted initial unemployment claims was 229,000, a decline of 5,000 from the previous week’s revised level of 234,000. The 4‑week moving average of weekly claims rose to 228,500, up 2,500 from the prior week’s revised average of 226,000. Both the weekly figure and the moving average were below the consensus forecast. The previous week’s data had been revised downward by 1,000 for the weekly figure and by 250 for the moving average.

title: ABD işsizlik maaşı başvuruları iki yılın zirvesinde
content: The U.S. Department of Labor reported that initial unemployment benefit claims for the week ending September 6, 2025 rose to 263,000, the highest level since October 2021, up from the previous week’s revised 236,000. Economists had expected 235,000. The seasonally adjusted initial claims increased by 27,000 from the prior week. The four‑week moving average of initial claims rose to 240,500 from 230,750. For the week ending August 30, the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate remained at 1.3%, unchanged from the previous week, with the number of insured unemployed at 1,939,000, unchanged from the prior week. The four‑week moving average of the unemployment rate fell to 1,945,750 from 1,946,500.

title: ABD'de işsizlik maaşı başvuruları 4 yılın en yüksek düzeyine ulaştı | Dünya Haberleri
content: The U.S. Department of Labor released weekly data on unemployment benefit claims. In the week ending September 6, first‑time claims rose by 27,000 to 263,000, the highest level since October 2021. Market expectations had been 235,000. The previous week’s figure was revised from 237,000 to 236,000. The 4‑week average claims increased by 9,750 to 240,500.

title: 《經濟》美國8月次周首次申請失業救濟人數增至23.5萬 遠高預期
content: The U.S. Department of Labor data shows that the number of people filing initial unemployment claims in the second week of August rose by 11,000 to 2.35 million, surpassing the market expectation of 2.25 million and marking the largest weekly increase in eight weeks. Meanwhile, the number of people continuing to receive unemployment benefits increased by 30,000 to 1.972 million, exceeding the expected 1.96 million and representing the largest rise since the end of 2021. The data indicates a slowdown in the U.S. labor market, with the rise in continuing claims dampening recruitment activity and intensifying the trend.
